Revert "enable mouse for tmux"

This reverts commit e5af3dd3fa7dab34692489e0c669fa3544135f0b.

I don't find myself using mouse in tmux that much, but what I _do_ find
myself doing is needing to select stuff to copy-and-paste to the
system clipboard, and when I have mouse mode enabled I need to
Option-click to do that. But these days I'm also fairly frequently using
terminal tabs _without_ tmux, and Option-click doesn't do as expected
there. So let's lose this Option-click muscle memory.

Add gh-pr-desc for converting commit messages to PR descriptions

Uses Claude to reformat a commit message for use as a GitHub PR
description: unwrapping hard-wrapped lines, collapsing loose lists
into tight lists, adding backticks around code identifiers, and
inlining numbered references. An LLM is needed because identifying
code identifiers and distinguishing references from other bracket
syntax (e.g. array indices) are both fuzzy tasks.

Add ghlite.nvim for reviewing GitHub PRs in Neovim

ghlite.nvim was chosen over alternatives like octo.nvim and
gh.nvim without much deliberation — it looked lightweight and
sufficient. It provides :GHLite* commands for PR review
workflows backed by the gh CLI.

The plugin's README suggests <leader>u as a keybinding prefix,
but that clashes with the existing vim-test bindings
(<leader>us for :TestSuite, <leader>ul for :TestLast). Instead,
<leader>pr was chosen as the prefix, giving <leader>prd for the
diff view and <leader>prc for leaving review comments.

Migrate from coc.nvim to Neovim native LSP

All done by Claude with minimal thought from me — I just needed to get
completion working for Swift again, and it seems to work. Here's its
commit message:

> Replace coc.nvim with the native Neovim LSP stack. The immediate
> trigger was coc-sourcekit being broken with Xcode 26 (it passes
> --stdio to sourcekit-lsp, which no longer accepts that flag), but
> coc.nvim was increasingly out of step with the Neovim ecosystem
> regardless — it runs its own Node.js process and ignores Neovim's
> built-in LSP client.
>
> The new stack:
>
> - nvim-lspconfig: provides server definitions (default cmd, filetypes,
>   root markers) so we don't have to spell them out. Servers are
>   configured and enabled via Neovim's native vim.lsp.config /
>   vim.lsp.enable API rather than lspconfig's deprecated
>   require('lspconfig').X.setup() framework.
>
> - mason.nvim + mason-lspconfig.nvim: auto-install and manage LSP
>   server binaries. ts_ls is installed automatically via mason.
>   sourcekit-lsp is NOT managed by mason — it uses the system binary
>   from Xcode (resolved via xcrun --find sourcekit-lsp).
>
> - blink.cmp: completion engine, chosen over nvim-cmp because it's a
>   single plugin rather than requiring several companions (cmp-nvim-lsp,
>   cmp-path, cmp-buffer, LuaSnip). Only LSP and path sources are
>   enabled (CoC config had around/buffer/file disabled). Keybindings
>   match the old CoC behaviour: Tab/S-Tab to navigate, CR to confirm,
>   C-Space to trigger.
>
> Keybindings preserve existing muscle memory from coc_config.vim:
> gd (definition), gy (type definition), gi (implementation),
> gr (references), K (hover), [g/]g (diagnostics), <leader>rn (rename),
> <leader>a (code action), <leader>qf (quickfix), <space>o (document
> symbols), <space>s (workspace symbols), <space>a (diagnostics list).
> Comments note Neovim 0.11 built-in equivalents where they exist.
>
> Dropped bindings that were CoC-specific or niche:
> - <leader>ac/as/re/r — covered by <leader>a
> - <leader>cl (CodeLens), <C-s> (selection range) — niche
> - if/af/ic/ac text objects — need treesitter-textobjects, not LSP
> - <C-f>/<C-b> float scroll — Neovim 0.11 handles natively
> - <space>e/c/j/k/p — CoC list commands with no LSP equivalent
> - :Fold — use native Neovim folding
>
> Also deletes coc_config.vim, coc-settings.json, the CocMenuSel
> highlight hack in the theme config, and rewords install.sh comments
> to remove coc.nvim references.
